title: Higher-order Boole summation over normed real vector spaces

problemStatement.formal: For a : ℕ → E with E a normed ℝ-vector space and Δ the forward difference, there exist Euler/tangent-number coefficients c_k with S(a,n,m) = Σ_{k<r} c_k((-1)^{n+k}Δ^k a_n − (-1)^{m+k}Δ^k a_m) + (-1)^r c_r S(Δ^r a,n,m) as an exact finite identity, and ‖S(a,n,m) − Σ_{k<r} c_k((-1)^{n+k}Δ^k a_n − (-1)^{m+k}Δ^k a_m)‖ ≤ |c_r| Σ_{j=n}^{m-1} ‖Δ^r a_j‖.
problemStatement.plain: The parent gallery entry proves the first-order Boole summation identity — the alternating-series analogue of Euler–Maclaurin — over any normed real vector space. This problem asks whether the higher-order version, which iterates the finite difference r times with Euler-number coefficients, admits the same order-free formalization and whether its remainder bound in terms of the r-th total variation Σ‖Δ^r a_j‖ holds. Success would cover complex- and operator-valued alternating sums with sharper error control.
whyMatters: Higher differences Δ^r a are much smaller than Δa for smooth sequences, giving sharper asymptotic estimates for complex Fourier and Dirichlet partial sums
Completes the order-free program: confirms whether the full Boole/Euler–Maclaurin alternating expansion ports to Banach-valued sequences
Yields a reusable arbitrary-order booleSum Lean API applicable to normed Dirichlet/Leibniz convergence tests and numerical series acceleration

proven: First-order Boole identity and total-variation remainder bound over a normed ℝ-vector space — verified entry alternating-series-boole-summation-oq-02 (the r=1 base case, 0 sorries, 0 axioms)
Real-valued first-order Boole identity with monotonicity refinement — parent alternating-series-boole-summation
Classical higher-order Boole summation for real/complex sequences (Boole 1860, Nörlund) — established but not formalized in iterated order-free form
open: Whether the r-th order identity holds verbatim as an exact finite identity over an arbitrary normed ℝ-module, and the exact Euler/tangent-number coefficients c_k that make it so
Whether the higher-order remainder bound |c_r|Σ‖Δ^r a_j‖ is the sharpest natural order-free estimate
Whether induction on the window or induction on the order r is the cleaner formalization route
knownResults.goal: Formalize over NormedSpace ℝ E the second-order Boole identity and its remainder bound as a concrete first target, then generalize to arbitrary order r by induction on the order; deliver the iterated finite difference Δ^r API and the coefficient recurrence.
